title: ACTIVATE DGPPN Attitudes, Clinician activity and prescription of Exercise – DGPPN
summary:
Physical activity can improve the mental and physical health of people with mental disorders. Although its benefits are well established, exercise is still not sufficiently recommended or prescribed in routine psychiatric care. Healthcare professionals play an important role in promoting physical activity. Their knowledge, attitudes and personal experiences may influence how often they recommend exercise to their patients.
The aim of this study is to investigate the knowledge and attitudes of healthcare professionals working in psychiatric care regarding physical activity and to assess how frequently they recommend or prescribe exercise as part of treatment. In addition, the study examines which patient characteristics and preferences influence the decision to recommend physical activity.
The study will take place during the congress of the German Association for Psychiatry, Psychotherapy, Psychosomatics and Neurology in Berlin in November 2026. Participating healthcare professionals will complete a web-based questionnaire and assess four standardised case scenarios involving different mental disorders, levels of illness severity, physical comorbidities and patient preferences regarding physical activity.
In addition, interested participants may voluntarily undergo a cycle ergometer test to assess their physical fitness. After completing the study, all participants will receive information material on promoting physical activity in people with mental disorders.
Three months after congress participation, participants who have voluntarily provided their email address will be invited to complete a brief online follow-up questionnaire to assess possible changes in their exercise recommendation and prescription practices.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Participation in the DGPPN Congress 2026
- Active involvement in psychiatric-psychotherapeutic patient care (in a medical, psychological, nursing, or complementary therapeutic capacity)
- Sufficient proficiency in German
- Capacity to consent and provision of voluntary, informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- No involvement in psychiatric or psychotherapeutic care
- Lack of capacity to provide consent or absence of consent
- Additionally, for the bicycle ergometer test: known blood pressure > 160 mmHg systolic or > 115 mmHg diastolic; resting heart rate > 100 beats per minute; significant shortness of breath; persistent cough; swelling in the feet, ankles, or calves; acute infection; recent surgery or injury; chest pain at rest or during physical exertion within the last month; bone or joint problems that worsen with physical activity; pregnancy; or any other known reason that precludes physical exertion
